title: Transform Self-Love into Empathy: The Law of Narcissism
coreMove: Redirect attention from your own image and hurt toward the other person's inner pressure before deciding what they owe you.
sourcePressure: This law treats narcissism as a spectrum and asks the reader to turn some self-love into empathy instead of using narcissism as an insult.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Using narcissism as a label for bad people instead of recognizing the ordinary pull of self-absorption in yourself.

exampleSpecs.domain: a documentary editor cutting an interview subject down to make herself look sharper
exampleSpecs.audience: a creative lead who mistakes control for vision
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the film loses the subject's real complexity
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the editor watches the raw answer again and removes her clever cut because the subject's pressure matters more than her own brilliance
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a timeline full of blue audio blocks on a dark editing screen

exampleSpecs.domain: a hospice volunteer who keeps telling comforting stories that center himself
exampleSpecs.audience: a helper learning that good intentions can still feed the ego
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a dying patient gets companionship or a performance
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after a visit falls flat, he counts how many sentences began with his own experience and rewrites the next visit around one question
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a volunteer badge lying beside an untouched paperback

exampleSpecs.domain: a youth orchestra conductor correcting a soloist too publicly
exampleSpecs.audience: a teacher whose standards are mixed with self-display
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the student hears craft or humiliation
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the conductor restates the correction privately by first naming what the player was trying to protect in the phrase
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a violin case open under a row of stage lights

exampleSpecs.domain: a boutique fitness instructor posting client transformations as proof of her own brand
exampleSpecs.audience: a coach with real skill and attention hunger
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether clients become people or props
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she changes the post from her own triumph caption to the client's stated goal and consented words
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a ring light reflected in a gym mirror

exampleSpecs.domain: a public defender impatient with a client who keeps missing calls
exampleSpecs.audience: an advocate whose frustration hides wounded competence
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether legal help collapses because the client feels unseen
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: before the next call, the defender writes the client's fear and schedule constraints beside the missed-call log
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a courthouse hallway bench with a cracked vinyl seat

exampleSpecs.domain: a tabletop game designer reading harsh playtest notes
exampleSpecs.audience: a maker whose identity is fused with the product
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether useful feedback gets dismissed as ignorance
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he predicts which note is just taste, then watches a new table hit the same confusion without knowing the first group
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a pile of cardboard tokens beside a rulebook draft

skillTargets: distinguish healthy self-regard from attention hunger

tryThisNowSpec: In one conversation today, summarize the other person's pressure in your own notes before you make your next point.

sourceAnchors.name: Stalin
sourceAnchors.detail: the source uses Stalin as the severe case of deep narcissism organized around loyalty, fear, control, and criticism as injury
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Stalin shows the end point of self-love that can no longer let other people remain fully real.

sourceAnchors.name: Tolstoy and Sonya
sourceAnchors.detail: the source uses Tolstoy and Sonya to show self-reference turning intimacy into a contest of injuries
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Tolstoy and Sonya bring the same distortion into the room where love should have made listening easier.

sourceAnchors.name: Shackleton
sourceAnchors.detail: the source uses Shackleton as a healthier model of strong self-belief that remains attentive to crew morale and fear
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Shackleton's authority holds because his self-belief still leaves room for the crew's reality.
